The image shows a soybean field with a clear contrast: several rows in the foreground are still green (green leaves, green stems) while the surrounding and background plants have fully matured and turned brown/tan — indicating they are harvest-ready. The green plants have abundant foliage and moist-looking green stems while neighboring rows are clearly at full maturity.

This matches **Green_stem_disorder** precisely: "All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature... stems remain moist while pods and seeds have ripened... green stems when neighboring plants are near harvest maturity."

No lesions, mold, pustules, or other pathogen signs are visible. The diagnostic feature is purely the green persistence of certain rows against a fully matured field background.
